target.title: fix: #94482 normalize cacheRetention 'standard' to 'short'
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveCacheRetention()` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-retention.ts` is the central gate for all cache retention values. It only recognized `"none"`, `"short"`, and `"long"`. When a user set `cacheRetention: "standard"` (valid in Anthropic API docs), the value fell through the family gate for non-`anthropic-direct` providers (e.g. `amazon-bedrock`) and was silently discarded — the explicit user config was treated as if unset.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `"standard"` → `"short"` normalization at the central gate, before the family check. This fixes the issue for ALL providers, not just Bedrock. The downstream Bedrock provider already handles `"short"` correctly, so no provider-side changes are needed.

## Evidence

### Unit tests (fresh run on PR branch `1a561fc`)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/prompt-cache-retention.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  8 passed (8)
   Start at  20:19:54
   Duration  309ms
```

All 8 tests pass, including the 2 new `"standard"` → `"short"` normalization tests:

| Test | Input | Provider | Expected | Result |
|------|-------|----------|----------|--------|
| standard → short (anthropic-direct) | `cacheRetention: "standard"` | `anthropic` | `"short"` | ✓ |
| standard → short (bedrock) | `cacheRetention: "standard"` | `amazon-bedrock` | `"short"` | ✓ |
| existing: none/short/long pass-through | various | various | passthrough | ✓ (6 tests) |

### Before/after behavior

- **Before**: `resolveCacheRetention({ cacheRetention: "standard" }, "amazon-bedrock", "bedrock-converse-stream", "us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6")` → `undefined` (fell through family gate)
- **After**: same call → `"short"` (normalized before family check)

## User Impact

Users who set `cacheRetention: "standard"` for Bedrock Claude models (following Anthropic API documentation) will now have their cache retention honored instead of silently discarded. No impact on existing `"short"`/`"long"`/`"none"` users.

Closes #94482
